document.title: Taliban Deliver Letter from Muttawakil; Say They Will Comply With Office Closing in New York (State 028054)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] The Taliban deliver a letter from Foreign Minister Muttawakil to Secretary Powell asking him to reconsider prior policies. They claim bin Laden is contained and that no evidence links him to terror plots, and hint at trading him for U.S. recognition. They say 80-90% of Afghans dislike him, and Taliban representative Noorullah Zadran says they 'wished your missiles had hit him'.

events.description: Mujahed and Zadran met Eastham, delivered Muttawakil letter to Powell, were told to close the Taliban New York office under UNSCR 1333/1267.
Press reporting from Islamabad indicated Muttawakil understood US intentions to implement UNSCR 1333.
State Department cable 028054 sent reporting the meeting.
Mujahed and Zadran meet Eastham, Lunstead and Cole at State Department; deliver Muttawakil letter to Powell; told to close Taliban New York office.
Mujahed says Taliban would comply with instruction to close New York office.
Mujahed reportedly told media after the meeting he was only instructed to restrict his movements.
Press reporting from Islamabad indicates Muttawakil understands the full meaning of U.S. intentions to implement UNSCR 1333.
State Department cable sent to Islamabad and other posts reporting the meeting.

key_claims: The Taliban's Muttawakil letter offered no new proposals on bin Ladin or compliance with UNSCR 1333.
Mujahed said he would comply with closing the New York office but later told press he was only to restrict his movements.
Mujahed and Zadran claimed most Taliban leaders wanted to be rid of bin Ladin.
The US warned it reserved the right to act in self-defense if bin Ladin was responsible for the Cole attack or planning another.
